answer: Each agent identity must periodically complete a fresh compute puzzle bound to its own public key, like a ship that can only dock at one wharf at dawn: the puzzle seed changes every epoch, so one machine cannot reuse work across identities. Running a thousand fake identities means paying a thousand puzzles worth of electricity and time, while one honest agent pays for one. The cost is visible like pigment in water, cheap to check, expensive to fake at scale.
